definition: Estimating per-pixel motion between two consecutive frames as a 2D displacement field.
details: Estimating per-pixel motion between two consecutive frames as a 2D displacement field. Networks such as FlowNet and RAFT supply motion cues for video understanding and tracking.

explainer.lead: It estimates per-pixel motion between two consecutive frames as a 2D displacement field. It supplies motion cues for video understanding and tracking.

tiers.eli5: It's like watching two photos taken a split second apart and noting which way each dot moved.
tiers.practitioner: Networks such as FlowNet and RAFT predict dense displacement fields for tracking and video analysis; large or occluded motion between frames is a common source of error.
tiers.paperLevel: Given consecutive frames, estimate a displacement vector per pixel forming a 2D field. Accuracy degrades where motion is large or pixels are occluded.

explainer.example: Between two video frames of a moving car, each pixel on the car is assigned a displacement vector pointing in the direction of travel.
